svg.title: MIRA Reference Architecture
svg.desc: Reference architecture and deployment flow for a Zello voice gateway, explicit curated procedure retrieval and general domain routing. One Foundry-native APIM gateway exposes a dedicated WebSocket voice API and native project HTTP API for router model calls. ClusterIP and downstream tool routes remain direct. WebSocket governance applies at handshake only. Voice and IQ application adapters connect to a Foundry prompt agent and a server tool runner. Fabric grounding selects Direct DAX or Fabric IQ Data Agent as alternative execution routes. GitHub governs approved Markdown export, release review, immutable Azure Managed Redis snapshots, CAS revision activation, Pub/Sub hints and startup/periodic router reconciliation. Local queries use a hydrated index and evidence-only LRU without per-query Redis calls. Dashed amber arrows represent asynchronous content publishing.
svg.text: AI copilot for frontline radio operations
VOICE OPERATIONS | GOVERNED KNOWLEDGE | FABRIC GROUNDING | CONTENT RELEASE PLANE
Go gateway | Zello voice (Opus codec) | local Whisper tiny.en
One active listener per radio channel
≤250 ms: skip “Standby.” | Publish results after acknowledgement
Clean speech text; follow-up detail retained; final audio buffered.
Direct ClusterIP; only routing / synthesis model calls use AI Gateway
No Fabric / Foundry / Work IQ lookup
Local index + LRU; no per-query Redis calls
Personal/live data is not in the local cache
Probes: /healthz startup | /readyz readiness + liveness (5 failed probes restart)
APIM Basic v2 | Auth, routing, request metrics
WebSocket: voice Entra identity + model restriction
Handshake only; original bearer; full-duplex audio
Router model calls; APIM MI authenticates backend
Operations adapter connects to grounding below
Direct tools: fixed delegated M365 identity
Not a personal identity for each radio speaker
Private workplace content stays outside corpus
Voice operations adapter: domain query + grounded result
IQ APPLICATION INTERFACE + FABRIC SEMANTIC GROUNDING
Shared application contract for voice and signed-in web clients; source selection and authorization stay explicit.
Server executes against semantic model; no Data Agent hop
Fabric IQ Data Agent MCP; authorized integration identity
Lakehouse / OneLake • PostgreSQL mirror • Databricks mirrored catalog
Approved source → immutable Redis snapshot → CAS revision pointer + Pub/Sub → validated atomic activation in running routers.
Download → validate hashes / scope / review / expiry → build index → atomic activation; invalidate old evidence.
Startup + periodic checks are required. Redis Pub/Sub is a lossy hint, not the correctness mechanism.
Runtime status / telemetry: active revision, source SHA, source_checked_at, activated_at, last successful reconciliation and lease / expiry.
Freshness follows serving runtime state, not pod annotations: no pod restart or image rebuild is required for content activation.
TLS + runtime read-only managed identity; separate publisher write authority. Redis stores snapshots / control, never private query data.
Redis transport outage: last-approved use only while unexpired and within refresh lease. Invalid / withdrawn authority fails closed.
Rollback: CAS pointer to an approved, nonwithdrawn, unexpired snapshot; reconcile and verify serving revision. Preserve original source metadata.
ACR images: separate code release. Redis excludes audio, prompts, private M365 content and Fabric results. No per-query Redis calls.
AI Gateway: model routes only; no response-cache link to Redis. Downstream tools stay direct. Procedure evidence retrieval is local.
PROCEDURE SCOPE: curated planning guidance; operational facts use explicitly selected live services.
Voice rendering still uses the AI Gateway.
Reference architecture and deployment flow • Explicit source authority • Governed content releases • Alternative Fabric execution modes
